world_news.headline: Politics live: RBA concedes Australians ‘furious’ about cost of living; Victorian energy bills may rise by $100 a year under Coalition
world_news.summary:
Follow the day’s news live

Albanese dismisses concerns over powers in digital duty of care bill

Anthony Albanese says the Nationals leader, Matt Canavan, is being “disingenuous” over his criticisms that the communications minister, Anika Wells, will have too much power to broaden the content that platforms will have to protect users from under the new digital duty of care legislation.

The eSafety commissioner will of course provide the advice, but Matt Canavan actually knows that he’s being disingenuous because all of these things will be disallowable. That is, will be up to the whole parliament, like the other previous laws have been.

Otherwise, what you’ve got to do in order to make a change, is to change the legislation, so to be coming forward over and over again.

world_news.headline: UK air traffic control problem strands hundreds of thousands of passengers
world_news.summary:
More than 1,000 flights cancelled as airlines call for overhaul of ATC system after third incident in just over three years

  • UK airport disruption: what are your rights?

Hundreds of thousands of air passengers had flights delayed or cancelled after another UK air traffic control technical glitch kept planes grounded for hours on Tuesday.

Airlines demanded action after a “technical issue” at the air traffic control services provider Nats caused the third large-scale stoppage in just over three years.
